guarantees.claim: For each share i in 0..NumShares-1, msg_masked[i] is combinationaly assigned as msg[i] XOR ({MsgWidth{msg_mask_en_i}} & msg_mask_permuted), effectively XORing msg with msg_mask_permuted when msg_mask_en_i is high, and with zero when low.

assumptions.claim: msg_mask_permuted must be a valid, unpredictable, and unbiased mask value generated externally to achieve effective side-channel resistance; its width must match MsgWidth.
assumptions.risk: If msg_mask_permuted is predictable, correlated with msg, or of incorrect width, the masking may be ineffective, potentially leading to side-channel leakage or simulation/synthesis errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The same mask value msg_mask_permuted is applied to all shares (msg[i] for all i) unconditionally when enabled. In a typical threshold implementation for side-channel resistance, each share should be masked with an independent random value to avoid cross-share leakage. This architecture may compromise the masking scheme.
uncertain_points.risk: If security relies on independent shares, reuse of the same mask across shares could create statistical dependencies exploitable by power analysis attacks.
